name: Die
description: A white six-sided plastic die with black pips.
notes: 16 mm on a side with the pips painted flush, opposite faces adding to seven; enamel-white draws the body because plastic-gloss-white read grey. Rolling it for a random number has no content field yet.

name: Poppy seed head
description: A green poppy seed head with a purple crown. Its sap is a strong sedative.
notes: 47 mm tall: a short stem, a round pod 28 mm across and a flat crown with eight ridges. leaf-green draws the pod and plant-purple the crown. The pod is drawn at a readable size; a much smaller one would be unreadable. Extracting its sap needs recipes.

name: Power converter
description: A small aluminium mains power unit with a cooling fan and three output leads.
notes: 150 by 100 mm and 60 mm tall: a bare aluminium case, a fan behind a wire guard, a mains socket and red switch on the front, a label on top and red, black and yellow leads out of the right side. The box counts the air round the leads. Using it in electronics needs recipes.

name: Processor board
description: A green circuit board with a large socketed processor chip in the middle.
notes: 150 by 110 mm: a green board with a white socket and a steel-lidded processor, memory and support chips, six capacitors, a pin header and a gold edge connector along the front. Using it in electronics needs recipes.

name: Radio repeater module
description: A grey metal module with two whip antennas, made to turn a radio station into an unattended relay.
notes: A case 200 mm wide, 80 mm tall and 125 mm deep with a black front panel, two carry handles, three status lamps, a capped data port, cooling fins behind and two rubber antennas 180 mm tall on top. The antennas add most of the box. Fitting it to a radio station needs a recipe or construction.

name: Length of light rail track
description: A short section of narrow-gauge track: two steel rails spiked to four timber sleepers.
notes: 1.2 m long with rails 600 mm apart, 64 mm tall with a worn bright head, spiked to four sleepers 900 by 150 mm and 60 mm thick. The box counts the air between the sleepers and rails. The iso tile needs --size 512 to read. The size is a placeholder for a thing too big for a pack; laying track needs construction.

name: Memory stick
description: A green computer memory stick with a row of black chips and a gold contact edge.
notes: 133 by 31 mm and 2 mm thick, lying flat with eight chips, a white label and a gold contact strip. The row id is ram_stick because row ids must be lowercase. Using it in electronics needs recipes.

name: Rebar
description: A rusty steel reinforcing bar. Heavy enough to swing or pound with.
notes: 800 mm long and 16 mm across, drawn plain in scrap-rusted: ribs at the 2 mm grain barely show, as the rebar bundle found. It lies along x and takes its grip on the bar. hammering 1 follows the brick. Swinging it as a weapon has no melee block in this draft. The ring stand is a different shape, so it has its own model and draft.

name: Ring stand
description: A laboratory stand: an iron base, an upright steel rod and a clamped support ring for holding a flask over a flame.
notes: It gets its own model, since it shares nothing of the bar's shape. 520 mm tall: a painted iron base 200 by 130 mm, a 12 mm rod, a clamp boss with a thumb screw and a 100 mm ring. The box counts the air round a tall rod. It brings no quality name in use yet; holding a vessel over heat would want one.

name: Signal receiver
description: A small aluminium box with an antenna jack and a stub antenna, made to pick up radio signals.
notes: 100 mm wide, 35 mm tall and 65 mm deep with screwed steel end plates, a gold jack and a short rubber antenna on the front, a green lamp, a label on top and a pin header behind. The box counts the air round the antenna. Using it in electronics needs recipes.

name: Refrigerant cylinder
description: A small sealed steel cylinder of refrigerant. It cannot be opened without the right valve.
notes: 90 mm across and 220 mm tall: a white steel body on a foot ring with a domed shoulder, a blue band, a brass valve and a black cap. The box counts the air round a round can. Charging a fridge or freezer from it needs recipes.

name: Prototype data card
description: A clear plastic card with a chip and gold traces set in it. It holds recorded data.
notes: 84 by 54 mm and 2 mm thick, lying flat: a clear card with a black chip under gold pads and four gold traces. The tile draws the card opaque; it stays see-through in the game. Reading it or handing it in needs content that does not exist yet.

name: Tin of rubber cement
description: A small tin of flexible rubber glue with a brush in the cap. It smells strongly of solvent.
notes: 64 mm across and 104 mm tall: a red can with a white band, a sloped shoulder and a ribbed black cap; the brush sits inside. The whole tin is one item, as for liquids. Gluing with it needs recipes; no adhesive quality name is in use yet.

name: Koji rice
description: Cooked rice overgrown with white mould and yeast, ready for brewing. Not good to eat as it is.
notes: A bare mound 120 mm across and 35 mm tall with patches of mould. paint-cream draws the rice and cloth-sage the mould. The mound is about 200 ml. Brewing with it needs recipes.

name: Crystal sample
description: A clear acrylic block with a small black crystal cast in its centre. It feels faintly warm.
notes: A 55 mm cube of plastic-clear around a six-sided obsidian crystal 14 mm across and 28 mm tall with a pointed top. The tile draws the block opaque and hides the crystal; it shows in the game. Its use in research has no content yet.

name: Sassafras root
description: A length of reddish-brown tree root with a sweet, spicy smell, used to flavour drinks.
notes: 220 mm long and 32 mm across at its cut end, tapering, with three flat side roots spreading in the ground plane. leather-chestnut draws the bark and wood-pine the cut face. The box counts the air round the spreading side roots. Brewing with it needs recipes.
